- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Companion planting is a great way to create a harmonious and thriving garden ecosystem.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Good companions for tomatoes include basil, oregano, marigold, borage, and chives.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Bad companions for tomatoes include fennel, potato, and members of the Brassica family (broccoli, cauliflower, kale).
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Good companions for basil include tomatoes, peppers, oregano, and marigold.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Basil can be sensitive to strong-scented herbs like sage and rosemary.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] General tips include planting marigold and nasturtium around the perimeter of the garden, avoiding planting members of the same plant family together, and considering the mature size of plants to prevent overcrowding.

- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Natural ways to deter slugs and snails include:
  1. Copper barriers
  2. Crushed eggshells

  4. Beer traps
  5. Companion planting with marigolds, chives, and garlic
  6. Physical barriers like copper mesh and fine-netting
  7. Diatomaceous earth
  8. Traps using lettuce or potato scraps
  9. Encouraging natural predators like toads and hedgehogs
  10. Keeping the garden clean
